author: El James’s
title: Great game - would recommend
content: I really love this game; it’s cozy and relaxing. I like that there’s no time limit or move limit; it would be very easy for the game devs to decide that the game needs stakes and say “you have to solve the puzzle in x amount of turns,” but I like that they know that this should only be a relaxing game. I only have two gripes, otherwise I would have given five stars. First gripe: some of the colors are too similar to each other and confuse me during levels, and I’m not even colorblind. Second gripe: the precision is too low. I’ll tap the screen and a good amount of the time it’ll register as though I tapped on a different part of the screen, selecting something far away from where I actually tapped. This is another reason why I’m glad there’s no move limit; if there was a limit to the number of moves you could make, the number of accidental moves I make due to the game selecting something I did not tap would certainly make me lose the level.

author: Dark-Starr
title: So relaxing
content:
This is a real chill and zen game. If you want to just sit and relax, but still want to do something on your phone that doesn't require complete focus or competition, this game is for you. Theres no time limit at all, so you're free to go any pace you want and there's no leaderboard, so you don't feel pressured into grinding for 1st place. 

Once the puzzle is complete, it's usually a super kawaii animal or chibi character and it's super cute. The ads are also very minuscule; they only pop up once you complete a puzzle but you can exit out in like 2 seconds, so it's not that big of a deal to me.

Overall, I would recommend this game to anyone who just wants to vibe and pass time.

author: Shrikex0r
title: Input lag makes the game nearly unplayable
content:
I enjoyed this game for a while, but recently it has become essentially unplayable due to input lag. Single presses get missed, and if you tap around the screen while lagged, several seconds later all the queued inputs will fire at once, selecting and deselecting colors repeatedly. Moving a zoomed-in canvas is similarly laggy, with a delay of several seconds before the game recognizes that a finger is being dragged. While dragging, it will also lose track of this fact and act as if a single press has been input, which de-selects the color you had active, or selects one you didn’t intend. 

Restarting the app or rebooting my device does not mitigate this behavior. No other app on my iPad behaves this way; there is something wrong with this one.

author: RainaJ7
title: As it says on the tin
content:
Compared to other puzzle/destressor games I’ve played, this one is the best so far. No timers, no limited moves; even if the jewel color placement is horrendous on some levels its still completable if you have the patience. The powerups are nice, and only ever used as a quality of life thing. (I personally love the brush). The adds at the end of each level are a touch annoying, but I will happily handle those as the game having adds means that it doesn’t have to push micro transactions down our throat (unlike certain other games). And that’s the best part- no micro transactions.

Truly if you just want a nice satisfying game, this is what you’re looking for.
